note: Flags never block a merge. Each flag states what is unverified or irregular, what the workspace shows, and what would resolve it. Source IDs refer to data/sources.json.

flags.title: Current market values are client estimates with no official valuation source
flags.detail: Client gives $3,100,000 (Property A) and $1,800,000 (Property B) as of Nov 2026. No appraisal or official index was retrieved. Every projection starts from these two numbers.
flags.action: Obtain a licensed appraisal or comparative market analysis for each property; re-run the model.

flags.title: Only 2025 values and a 2026 projection are carried; the multi-year history was not retained
flags.detail: Client assessed value 2025 = $539,743; tax 2025 = $7,207 (effective 1.335%, computed). The 2026 figure $550,537 is a +2% projection (539,743 x 1.02 = 550,537.86), not an official 2026-27 roll value. The earlier multi-year table was not retained in the workspace, so it is not reproduced here.
flags.action: Confirm the 2026-27 roll value and the bill on the Santa Clara County tax bill; re-supply the earlier years if needed.

flags.title: Effective tax rate of 2.13% is irregular for San Francisco
flags.detail: Client tax 2025 = $2,439 on assessed value $114,248 (2.135%). A 1% general levy would give about $1,142, leaving about $1,297 per year from bonds, special taxes or direct assessments. That split cannot be verified without the bill. The model keeps 2.13% as base and 1% as a lower bound.
flags.action: Read the SF secured tax bill line by line (levies, bonds, special taxes, direct assessments).

flags.title: Insurance premiums are client estimates; official premium results could not be read
flags.detail: Client guesses $1,500 per year for each property. A secondary summary cites the CDI February 2026 statewide average as $1,571 (national $1,512); that CDI snapshot itself was not opened. The CDI 2026 tool lists 'SANTA CLARA CUPERTINO' and 'SAN FRANCISCO - Sunset District', but premium results did not render. A 3-unit building with rentals usually needs a landlord or multi-unit policy, which is a different product.
flags.action: Get written quotes for the actual structure, occupancy and coverage; check the CDI snapshot directly.

flags.title: Client 'solar profit' conflicts with the fixed monthly charge
flags.detail: Client says the solar credit nets about $10-$20 per month. CPUC material cites a Base Services Charge of about $24.15 per month (standard), and secondary summaries of PG&E and SCE say solar credits cannot offset it. Whether the system is on net billing (Solar Billing Plan) or an older tariff is unknown. The Cupertino electric utility and tariff are also not confirmed on an official source.
flags.action: Pull 12 months of bills, the interconnection date and the tariff name; confirm the fixed charge line item.

flags.title: Top federal estate tax rate (40%) not confirmed on an official page
flags.detail: The IRS estate-tax page used here does not state the rate. Secondary sources cite 40% under IRC 2001(c). The rate is not used in any calculation because the estate is assumed to be below the $15M exclusion.
flags.action: Confirm the rate in IRC 2001(c) or the Form 706 instructions.

flags.title: Basis step-up wording not read on an official page
flags.detail: IRS Topic 703 points to Publication 551 for inherited property. The step-up to date-of-death value (IRC 1014) is used in the sale scenarios, but the official wording was not read in this session.
flags.action: Read IRS Publication 551 (inherited property) and confirm the basis rule with the estate's tax preparer.

flags.title: 1% MHST above $1,000,000 not confirmed on an official page
flags.detail: The FTB schedule PDF lists brackets up to 12.3%, but the surcharge is not printed there. Secondary sources describe a 1% surcharge. Only income above $1M is affected, so the model does not use it.
flags.action: Confirm against the statute and Form 540 instructions.

flags.title: SF Treasurer deadlines not confirmed; secondary sources conflict on second installment
flags.detail: sftreasurer.org pages returned 404 in this session. Secondary sources say the first installment is due Nov 1 and delinquent after Dec 10, 2026, and the second is due Feb 1 and delinquent after Apr 10, 2027. One source says Apr 12, 2027 because Apr 10, 2027 is a Saturday (confirmed: Saturday).
flags.action: Check the printed SF bill and sf.gov Treasurer pages when the 2026-27 bill arrives.

flags.title: Santa Clara second-installment date not confirmed officially
flags.detail: The DTAC page confirms the 2026-27 first installment must be paid or postmarked by Dec 10, 2026. Secondary sources say the second installment is due Feb 1 and delinquent after Apr 10, but no official page confirmed it.
flags.action: Check the printed Santa Clara bill.

flags.title: Water and electricity amounts are client ranges; comparisons are not like-for-like
flags.detail: Cupertino water $100-$150 per month (client). A San Jose Water advice letter (AL 628-A) lists a typical 10 CCF residential bill of $141.73 from July 1, 2026 as filed, which falls inside the range. San Francisco: client water and sewer $330-$400 per month for three units, compared with SFPUC's average single-family combined bill of $171 per month (FY26), which is a different building type. San Francisco electricity $30-$70 per month is unverified.
flags.action: Use 12 months of actual bills for each property.

flags.title: Rate filings are not confirmed as approved or in effect
flags.detail: AL 628-A is an advice letter; its approval status was not confirmed. The SFPUC presentation labels FY27 and FY28 increases as proposed; secondary sources report adoption in April 2026. Which water utility serves Property A was not confirmed on an official source beyond the tariff area described in the filing.
flags.action: Check the CPUC advice-letter status and the SFPUC adopted rate schedule.

flags.title: City transfer taxes are not included in sale costs
flags.detail: Only the county documentary transfer tax ($1.10 per $1,000) is included, from R&TC 11911. City or SF transfer taxes, if any, were not verified, so net sale proceeds may be overstated slightly.
flags.action: Confirm city and SF transfer-tax rates with the title company.

flags.title: Prop 40 result is preliminary; applicability is unverified
flags.detail: Only early returns (Nov 3, 2026) and secondary summaries were found. The measure reportedly applies only to net worth of $1B or more and excludes real estate, which was not verified on an official page. It is listed for awareness only.
flags.action: Check the certified statewide results after certification and the measure text.

flags.title: Key modeling assumptions have no official source
flags.detail: Maintenance (0.5% of value for Cupertino; 1.0% for SF), 5% brokerage, investment returns (4%, 6%, 8%), appreciation (0%, 2.5%, 4%), inflation scenarios (2.0%, 2.5%, 3.7%), and the heir's tax profile are planning choices. They drive the results and are shown with sensitivities on the projections page.
flags.action: Replace with the household's own figures and re-run data/inputs.json through scripts/model.py.

flags.title: Rent figure and rent-control status unverified
flags.detail: Client rent is $7,150 per month for two units (not verified). The 1.6% cap applies only to units covered by the local Rent Ordinance (S15). Civil Code 1947.12 exempts some housing, including units with a certificate of occupancy within 15 years (S27). Building age and coverage were not confirmed. The model uses 1.6% growth for the base case and inflation for the high case.
flags.action: Check the Rent Board unit listing and the leases; confirm coverage and any banked increases.

flags.title: Allocation of the Prop 19 exclusion across units is assumed
flags.detail: BOE LTA 2026/026 says only the unit occupied as principal residence qualifies, and the other units are reassessed at full cash value. The assessor decides how value is split. The model assumes one-third to the occupied unit, which is a planning assumption.
flags.action: Ask the assessor for the allocation method before relying on the hybrid result.

flags.title: Indexing of the $1,044,586 limit after 2027 is assumed
flags.detail: BOE adjusts the limit for inflation every two years; the next adjustment is February 2027 (S04). The model indexes it with inflation. Without indexing, the Property A live-case value in the base illustration falls by about $0.09M in real 2026 dollars.
flags.action: Re-run the model after each BOE adjustment.

flags.title: Heir marginal tax rates are assumed
flags.detail: The model uses 24% federal ordinary, 9.3% CA and 3.8% NIIT (total 37.1% on net rental income). The heirs' actual brackets are not known. CA rates are from the 2026 FTB schedule (S24); NIIT from IRS Topic 559 (S23).
flags.action: Re-run with each heir's actual bracket.

flags.title: Other estate assets unknown
flags.detail: The two client-estimated values total about $4.9M, below the $15M basic exclusion for 2026 (S01). Other assets, debts, and lifetime gifts are unknown, so the federal filing position cannot be confirmed.
flags.action: Prepare a total estate inventory; check portability and any Form 706 requirement with the estate's advisers.

flags.title: Some official sources were only partly read
flags.detail: BOE LTA 2026/026 chunks 8-10 (grandparent section and appeals) were not read. IRS Pub 523 and 527 were checked for structure only; the $250,000/$500,000 exclusion amounts were not read on the current official page. FHFA house-price data was not retrieved. The CDI statewide snapshot was not opened. The Santa Clara county rent-cap figure is secondary only.
flags.action: Complete the reads and update the facts register.

flags.title: Projection rounding in the client's 2026 assessed value
flags.detail: 539,743 x 1.02 = 550,537.86; the client figure of $550,537 is truncated, not rounded. The difference is immaterial but is recorded for completeness.
flags.action: None needed beyond the note.

flags.title: Federal estate tax repeal bills are pending
flags.detail: S.587 and H.R.1301 (Death Tax Repeal Act of 2025) were introduced Feb 13, 2025 and referred to committee. The congress.gov snapshot used here shows no later action, but the status may have changed.
flags.action: Check congress.gov before relying on the current status.

flags.title: What this public site omits on purpose
flags.detail: No names, street addresses, parcel numbers, account details, owner details or precise ZIP codes appear on the site. Properties are identified only as Property A (Cupertino, Santa Clara County) and Property B (San Francisco).
flags.action: None; this is a privacy control.

flags.title: Overlapping analysis at /docs/ (session 340c906c) uses different assumptions
flags.detail: Two analyses are published from this repository: the root site (session c1b5796b, data in data/ia/) and the /docs/ site merged to main by session 340c906c (data in data/ and docs/data/). They share the same questions but use different assumptions and do not agree on every figure (for example, the 2045 Property A tax and the break-even rent). Neither set is verified; both are labelled as assumption-based projections. The owner should decide which set to keep as the single published analysis.
flags.action: Owner to choose one published analysis or reconcile the assumptions; no figure is changed by this build.
